summary: Audit column after is reserved
detail: E_QUARRY_RESERVED: after is a reserved word; check provided an exact rename suggestion.
workaround: Renamed audit columns previousLimit and newLimit.
suggested_fix: Allow keyword columns where syntax is unambiguous, or retain the helpful diagnostic.

summary: Role-gated private scan cannot prove complete capacity
detail: E_STRUCTURAL_FANOUT on assignLane sum; a require role guard does not make the population readable. Diagnostic explicitly recommended a maintained aggregate.
workaround: Added a purser-readable laneLength aggregate and used its complete total.
suggested_fix: Recognize guards that prove a read-rule role branch, while retaining safe refusal for unknown overlap.

summary: Sum view filter ordering
detail: E_QUARRY_SYNTAX: a sum names its value before its filter; checker printed exact replacement.
workaround: Applied the diagnostic rewrite.
suggested_fix: No change needed; good error.

detail: grant mutation upserted profiles+roles; profiles insert rule was owner-only so every grant rolled back with E_RULE. My rule was wrong, but the failure (failed E_RULE on grant) did not name the profiles clause; had to reason it out. snapback4 why recent is the documented path.
summary: Mutation rollback names the mutation require, not the failing table clause
suggested_fix: Include the refusing table/clause in mutation failure details on dev

summary: Optional deadline comparisons require explicit narrowing
detail: E_QUARRY_TYPE: > needs present operands; got time and time ?
workaround: Added dueAt null guard before comparisons.
suggested_fix: Diagnostic already provides a useful rewrite.

summary: Time-dependent courier audience needs durable lifetime grants
detail: Rules exclude now; a courier must lose yesterday’s row and photo access but clinics and labs retain records.
workaround: Added courierGrants with not before/expire and keyed read-rule probes; tested row and asset expiry.
suggested_fix: Provide a documented mixed permanent-plus-daily audience recipe.

summary: Killing npm wrapper orphaned the serve binary; store stayed busy
detail: SIGTERM to the npm wrapper pid left the snapback4 serve child alive holding deployment/store.sqlite; the next start refused E_STORE_BUSY. The refusal text was excellent: it named the owner URL, pid, and remedy.
workaround: Signalled the exact leftover serve pid, then always signal the process group (bash -c 'kill -TERM -PGID'); scripts own children via proof-kit cleanup() in finally.
suggested_fix: Keep the E_STORE_BUSY message as-is; it is a model diagnostic. Optionally document that serve double-forks past an npm wrapper so wrappers must forward signals to the group.

summary: Atomic firing transitions need a declared fanout cap
detail: E_QUARRY_FANOUT: pieces has no cap over this prefix; a count guard is not a static product cap. Diagnostic gave an exact cap rewrite.
workaround: Declare a 30-piece cap per firing.
suggested_fix: Explain optional/null cap groups prominently in bounds documentation.

summary: Reference-based owner audience prevents bounded staff fanout
detail: E_STRUCTURAL_FANOUT rejected firingLoads with .piece.owner = viewer or staff, even behind an explicit staff require.
workaround: Copy immutable owner onto firingLoads and use its direct owner audience.
suggested_fix: Recognize uniform privileged branches when the other branch traverses a parent reference.

summary: Negative-probe advisories cannot establish role-helper visibility
detail: check reports N_UNREADABLE_PROBE for six queries/guards even though their roles give complete visibility to each table or marker row concerned. The advisory is useful for hidden-row bugs but conservative here.
workaround: Keep the notes visible and test every caller role, private-log audience and exact marker expiry over the live API.
suggested_fix: Prove role-helper implications where possible or identify the exact unproved audience branch.

summary: Rule comparison rejects required principal against optional principal
detail: E_QUARRY_TYPE: rule comparison joins principal with principal ?; a principal value cannot equal a value that may be null
workaround: Add explicit non-null guard on the assigned subtenant.
suggested_fix: Show a guard-based rewrite when it can narrow optional fields.

summary: Non-null guard did not narrow optional principal in a rule
detail: Adding .listing.subtenant != null still produced E_QUARRY_TYPE at the following comparison
workaround: Compare the optional assigned principal directly with viewer; the inserted subtenant already equals viewer
suggested_fix: Support guarded optional-field narrowing in rule comparisons.

summary: Unreadable-probe advisories require manual authorization review
detail: check passes but warns N_UNREADABLE_PROBE for assignSubtenant and book even with preceding office/matched-subtenant guards; uniqueness is an additional backstop
workaround: Reviewed the grants and proved duplicate booking/post-booking reassignment refusals on dev and serve; retained the conservative notes
suggested_fix: Use preceding role and audience guards to suppress advisories when read authority is established.

summary: A director-authorized transfer scan still needs all audience fields pinned
detail: E_STRUCTURAL_FANOUT: the mutation page read rule is not uniformly decided by its prefix, despite a director require before the loop.
workaround: Pin the member, old part, and singer principal in transfer scans.
suggested_fix: Use dominating role guards when proving scan uniformity or show an exact role-transfer recipe.

summary: Conservative completeness notes persist on role-branched track and roster queries
detail: check reports N_NEVER_COMPLETE and N_CONDITIONAL_COMPLETE even with a roster-role branch and own-part predicate; timed release existence is an additional nonuniform policy input.
workaround: Use cursor pages, display partial/loading/refusal states, and verify the actual audiences via direct row and asset tests. Keep live policy rules intact.
suggested_fix: Explain which branch and exact policy dependency prevents completeness, and offer a compiled recipe combining timed disclosure, roles, and protected asset homes.

summary: Optional row lookup makes bool conditional nullable
detail: E_QUARRY_TYPE: a conditional value needs a bool condition, got bool ? when reading policy by key.
workaround: Compared the optional bool to true as the diagnostic advised.
suggested_fix: Keep this useful rewrite diagnostic.

summary: E_QUARRY_RULE_HOP forced denormalizing group onto contents table
detail: Read rule exists users[principal=viewer, groupName=.box.groupName] refused: read rules cannot hop references. check printed exact span plus a concrete rewrite (copy groupName, verify in insert rule), which compiled first try.
workaround: Added groupName copy to contents with exists boxes[.box, groupName=.groupName] insert check; moveBox updates both atomically.
suggested_fix: Nothing broken; keep the rewrite quality. A cookbook note that group-scoped privacy implies a denormalized copy column would preempt the surprise.

summary: service:ops grant failed E_RULE because service could not read hidden roster row
detail: grantManager as service:ops took the insert branch (users[who] hidden from service) and the insert then refused as clobber-protection on the unreadable existing row. E_RULE text did not say the row was hidden vs truly absent.
workaround: Added viewer=service:ops to the users read rule per the ops-seat bootstrap recipe.
suggested_fix: When a write is refused due to a hidden-key conflict, name that the key holder is hidden from the caller (distinct from absent).

summary: Used helper instead of fn in Quarry
detail: E_QUARRY_SYNTAX: unexpected top-level helper. The programs card mentioned helpers without its declaration spelling.
workaround: Read language section 8 and changed declaration to fn.
suggested_fix: Include fn declaration syntax in the programs card.

summary: Private interval conflicts need a separate occupancy model
detail: The totals guide explains that inline count reads only authorized rows; arbitrary counts over private bookings cannot safely arbitrate conflicts. A generic interval exclusion constraint would avoid extra data modeling.
workaround: Use private quarter-hour occupancy cells, a maintained count per cell, and unique tick keys. This keeps booking identities private and checks conflicts atomically.
suggested_fix: Document a private temporal-reservation recipe, or provide an exclusion/overlap constraint that evaluates all rows without exposing them.

summary: kill -TERM -PID of detached probe killed my own shell instead
detail: After setsid -f launch, pgrep found the probe PID but kill -TERM -PID terminated the tool-call shell (signal 15) rather than just the probe group; serve/static children survived and held 21150/21151.
workaround: Enumerate exact PIDs with directory-qualified command lines (ps -eo pid,args | grep <app-dir>) and kill -TERM each PID individually; verified ports free afterwards.
suggested_fix: Document that proof-kit children should be stopped via their stop() handles inside scripts, and warn against group-kill from shared shells.

summary: Unpinned role-filtered pages cannot certify completeness
detail: check passed but N_NEVER_COMPLETE warned that participant and nurse diary pages could stay capped despite row authorization.
workaround: Pin participant reads to enrollment; nurses choose an assigned participant; investigator and manager have complete global pages.
suggested_fix: Offer a complete role-aware multi-owner query recipe adjacent to the basic role examples.

summary: Handle format excludes normal clinical participant codes
detail: Enrollment refused E_INPUT: code must be a handle: lowercase letters, digits and underscores. I had applied format handle to T017-1.
workaround: Use bounded text for study participant codes; codes are assigned only by the operator service.
suggested_fix: The existing diagnostic was clear; show allowed characters beside format handle in the cheatsheet.

summary: Completeness advice describes an unused global branch for participant callers
detail: N_NEVER_COMPLETE still says participant and nurse diary pages are capped after adding explicit role branches. Live pinned participant/nurse requests actually return complete:true, cut:null, next:null.
workaround: Read check --verbose, inspect actual envelopes for all four roles, and retain scoped branches.
suggested_fix: Make completeness analysis path-sensitive across role branches, or identify precisely which branch produces each advisory.

summary: Nested read rules and cascade caps need explicit modeling
detail: E_QUARRY_RULE_HOP on note clip/day and agent-client read predicates; E_CASCADE_BOUND with 2000 notes per clip.
workaround: Try read through clip and bound notes to 400 per clip.
suggested_fix: Explain mutable parent authority inheritance together with hop and cascade restrictions in first-app docs.

summary: N_IMMUTABLE_PATCH rewrite inapplicable when the immutable value is provably viewer
detail: check note on addListing upsert: 'omit owner from the patch if another value may update this row' — but owner is required on the insert path and always equals viewer (the only writer the rules admit), so the rewrite cannot apply. Note is advisory and check passes, but it reads like required action.
workaround: Kept owner in the upsert (correct: insert needs it, updates can only come from the same owner); ignored the advisory.
suggested_fix: Suppress N_IMMUTABLE_PATCH when the patched immutable column is provably equal to viewer and the table's update rule admits only that writer.

summary: check refused column named `by` (reserved word)
detail: E_QUARRY_RESERVED with an exact rewrite (rename the column). Expected friction for a new grammar; the diagnostic named the fix.
workaround: Renamed waivers.by to waivedBy.
suggested_fix: Nothing; the diagnostic is already exemplary.

summary: Positional members[viewer, viewer] probe named no unique key
detail: E_QUARRY_POSITIONAL_SCAN on 5 rules using exists members[viewer, viewer]; two principals match no declared key (composite is team+student). Expected the compiler to say which keys were tried; it pointed at guide reads instead.
workaround: Used exists members[viewer] (binds unique student) for any-membership and members[.team, viewer] (binds composite) for team-scoped probes.
suggested_fix: Include the tried key shapes in E_QUARRY_POSITIONAL_SCAN, e.g. 'keys: (team, student), (student)'.

summary: N_NEVER_COMPLETE capped verdict on team-pinned score pages
detail: Queries pinning .team but readable by several audiences (judge/coach/student/director) get a static capped verdict; the runtime page may report complete:false with full data. Had to read why N_NEVER_COMPLETE and design assertions/UI around data rather than the complete flag.
workaround: Acceptance asserts on data contents; UI renders partial pages with their rows (ScoreRows for both present and partial).
suggested_fix: Document the recommended client pattern (render partial-with-data as data) next to N_NEVER_COMPLETE, since multi-audience pages are the common case for role-gated queries.

summary: Hidden unique-key collision returns E_RULE rather than E_CONSTRAINT
detail: Acceptance expected E_CONSTRAINT for a duplicate sample number held by another brewer. Snapback returned E_RULE with a long diagnostic covering authorization, uniqueness, cap groups and physical work allowance. The privacy-preserving behavior is correct, but the diagnostic combines many explanations.
workaround: Assert E_RULE for a collision against a hidden row; retain E_CONSTRAINT checks for visible duplicates.
suggested_fix: Document hidden uniqueness refusal prominently and shorten the public diagnostic while retaining detailed local explanations.

detail: POST /seed with body {roles:[...]} refused 400 E_INPUT; message said: 'seed takes a JSON array of {table, row}'. Retried as [{table,row}] and 6 rows seeded.
summary: /seed body shape had to be discovered from a refusal message
suggested_fix: Show the /seed body shape in `guide testing` next to the loadFixtures//dev/reset recipe.
workaround: Reshaped the seed body to [{table:'roles',row:{...}}] per the refusal text.

detail: check passed with 4 N_MAINTAIN_DELTA notes ('may disclose the delta of a hidden tasks row'). `why` explained the channel, but it took a minute to convince myself it was benign: the views are readable only by lead/controller, who already read every source row, so no hidden row exists for their audience.
summary: N_MAINTAIN_DELTA notes need a moment to triage as benign
suggested_fix: When the view's read audience already reads every source row, say so in the note ('no hidden rows for this audience') instead of a generic review flag.

summary: Global count view reads by bare name, not keyed
detail: roleCount[] refused with E_QUARRY_TYPE: 'roleCount is one global maintained scalar, not a group table'; rewrite said read it by bare name (return roleCount). Expected keyed read like grouped counts.
workaround: Used bare `roleCount` in bootstrapProducer require.
suggested_fix: Mention ungrouped-count read syntax in guide totals/cheatsheet.

summary: Compiler cannot prove a coordinator grant makes the overdue-loan probe complete
detail: N_UNREADABLE_PROBE remains on restore after require exists roles[viewer, role = coordinator]. Diagnostic acknowledges a readable roles row but cannot connect it to loans read rule.
workaround: Retain explicit guard and test restoration refusal for both coordinators against overdue loans owned by two different borrowers.
suggested_fix: Track established roster predicates through a require so this common role guard can be proven.

summary: Schema check also validates stale acceptance-store adoption
detail: Adding required charges.tunerName caused E_ADOPT against two rows left by acceptance. The diagnostic clearly suggested optional/default/backfill.
workaround: Added a literal fallback for historical rows; all new records store the signed-in tuner name.
suggested_fix: Make the store used by check more prominent in normal output; the migration diagnostic itself was helpful.

summary: Revision-validated timed route publications produce a potentially incomplete scan
detail: N_NEVER_COMPLETE on myRoute: the compiler cannot prove a uniform audience because each publication probes booking address, revision, piano and window. Immutable publication revisions avoid returning stale addresses after reassignment or editing, but require a cross-table per-row rule.
workaround: Keep the rule intact, paginate with usePage, expose partial-result metadata in the UI, and acceptance-test that only the latest matching publication is returned.
suggested_fix: A native current-source publication construct or planner proof for unique-reference revision validation would simplify this common privacy pattern.

summary: Read rules cannot traverse team reference; read-through forbids mutable expiry
detail: E_QUARRY_RULE_HOP on .recording.team and E_READ_THROUGH: recordings.expiresAt is a captured deadline and must be immutable. Pinning needs a mutable deadline.
workaround: Copy immutable team into notes/reviews, validate it against recording in insert rule, and explicitly probe live parent in read rule.
suggested_fix: Document a pin/unpin retention recipe with child privacy; consider supporting live reference audience inheritance.

summary: Conservative completeness/read-probe advisories remain after access tests pass
detail: N_NEVER_COMPLETE on recordingNotes coach branch (missing staffOnly pin) and N_UNREADABLE_PROBE on startReview despite a live readable parent. Branching notes by role and pinning team removed part of the warning but not all.
workaround: Pin team/public-note predicates, bound notes with a 1000-per-recording cap, assert the full visibility matrix in acceptance, retain advisory evidence.
suggested_fix: Recognize role-implied visibility and parent/probe implications, or show a concise exact condition that would prove these safe cases complete.

summary: Staff enrollment needs a separately authored operator-only roster mutation
detail: Signup creates an account without a product role. Implementing three trusted staff roles required a roster table, service:ops minting and provisioning, then token revocation in the setup script.
workaround: Followed the documented first-admin service-seat recipe; ordinary clients cannot provision staff.
suggested_fix: Provide a small password-account plus trusted-role-enrollment starter and reusable provisioning helper.

summary: Cross-holder apply refused NOT_FOUND, not the authored NOT_YOUR_SLIP
detail: slips[slip] lookup hides unreadable rows, so the asserted lookup fires NOT_FOUND before the require. This is the documented ladder, but while writing the test I expected the require code; NOT_FOUND is the better privacy behavior.
workaround: Assert NOT_FOUND for cross-holder access; assert NOT_YOUR_SLIP via a staff caller who can read the slip.
suggested_fix: Add one line to guide refusals: asserted lookups on hidden rows beat later requires, with this exact cross-owner example.

summary: elif rejected; rewrite names nested else-if
detail: check reported E_QUARRY_UNSUPPORTED: elif is not part of Snapback 4, rewrite: else if cond:. Nested else/if compiled cleanly.
workaround: Rewrote joinAs/promote with nested else/if blocks.
suggested_fix: Accept elif as sugar for nested else/if, or keep the error (it was clear and fast).

summary: No client-side money-arg example found
detail: Quarry has money/decimal types but no crisp example of passing money arguments from the JS client, so amounts stayed int cents.
workaround: Used int 1..10000000 cents with $100 = 10000 boundary.
suggested_fix: One money-typed mutation example in guide types or cheatsheet.

summary: Atomic roster publication requires an explicit population bound
detail: E_QUARRY_FANOUT refused looping all children and future rides without product caps. Diagnostic gave useful cap and chunked-job alternatives.
workaround: Publish one child/day per operation; permanent changes apply when a daily roster is published.
suggested_fix: Provide a small batched-operation recipe for roster-like apps without arbitrary population caps.

summary: --fresh aliases --memory rather than creating a disposable disk store
detail: Retrying token mint against dev --fresh produced the same no-store diagnostic. dev --help explicitly documents both flags as temporary-store aliases.
workaround: Copy schema into a unique .scratch project and start default disk-backed dev there. The service token CLI then works.
suggested_fix: Add a supported --store or isolated-project option to token/dev for repeatable service-auth integration tests.

summary: Role grants are repeated in table rules and operation guards
detail: The implementation repeats roster predicates in the item/claim table rules and in require guards for clear refusal codes. This was straightforward but verbose; program roster reads and rule roster probes also have deliberately different visibility semantics.
workaround: Used the documented unique principal roster and explicit operation guards, then tested each role and guessed ID.
suggested_fix: Provide a compact password-account hotel/helpdesk example showing role provisioning, private inventory, and readable refusal guards together.

summary: Cross-client review queue cannot certify completeness
detail: check emitted N_NEVER_COMPLETE: query reviewQueue missing pin .client. The membership-based read rule needs a client scope as well as the language.
workaround: Scope each live queue to a selected assigned client and pin client in the query.
suggested_fix: Provide a documented complete multi-membership inbox pattern.

detail: First check on a schema with on-delete-cascade children refused E_CASCADE_BOUND: delete routes needs a product bound, with rewrite to add cap N by route on both children. Expected a plain cascade to compile; the reservation concept was new.
summary: Cascade edges require product caps (E_CASCADE_BOUND)
suggested_fix: Keep the error but mention cap-bounded cascade in guide writes near the delete recipe, not only in the diagnostic.
workaround: Added cap 300 by route on ascents and cap 100 by route on suggestions; check clean.

summary: Cascade onto maintained-sum source refused; needed explicit loop deletes
detail: check: E_REFERENCE_ACTION on items.drop/items.fridge (on delete cascade into a maintained sum source) + E_CASCADE_BOUND on drops.fridge. The rewrite named restrict/keep and the job-unwind recipe; guide programs documents for-loops in mutations. Expected cascade to just work; instead restructured to restrict + explicit deletes in removeFridge.
workaround: Changed all refs to on delete restrict, added caps, delete children explicitly with for loops in removeFridge.
suggested_fix: Keep the refusal, but the E_CASCADE_BOUND rewrite could mention the mutation-loop alternative alongside the job recipe for small fan-outs.

summary: Mutation require passed but table rule refused coordinator addItem with generic E_RULE
detail: addItem mutation allowed coordinator override via require, but items insert rule admitted only the drop's volunteer. Write failed E_RULE naming only the layer ('table authorization layer ... does not admit this viewer'). Took reading rule-recipes to realize BOTH layers must admit; nothing pointed at the specific conjunct.
workaround: Widened the table insert rule with an explicit coordinator arm.
suggested_fix: In dev, name the failing rule clause/conjunct in the E_RULE message or snapback4 why recent (e.g. which exists probe was false).

summary: Wrong expectation: hidden drop lookup is NOT_FOUND, not NOT_HOST
detail: Expected host2 dropItems(other drop) to refuse NOT_HOST like fridgeDrops does, but the lookup target (drops) is hidden to host2 so the engine correctly answers NOT_FOUND before the require runs. Refusal ladder in guide testing documents exactly this.
workaround: Corrected expectation to NOT_FOUND with a comment.
suggested_fix: None; docs already cover it.

summary: Intentional owner aggregate disclosure produces repeated advisory notes
detail: N_MAINTAIN_DELTA is reported for monthlyAlarms and monthlyEscalations. The wider owner aggregate audience is exactly the requested feature, so each check needs the same human interpretation.
workaround: Reviewed the disclosure and documented the intended owner-only aggregate channel. Kept the useful notes visible.
suggested_fix: Provide an obvious acknowledgement mechanism for an intentionally broader aggregate audience directly in the diagnostic rewrite.

summary: Optional time comparison needs explicit narrowing
detail: check rejected a.deadline > now and <= now because deadline is optional. Diagnostic supplied the exact null-coalescing rewrite.
workaround: Use (a.deadline ?? 0) in deadline comparisons.
suggested_fix: Keep these diagnostics; they were helpful.

summary: Completeness advice is hard to apply to blind review visibility
detail: After adding cursors, check retains N_NEVER_COMPLETE for applicationScores and N_CONDITIONAL_COMPLETE for reservations. A pin on panelist would hide other panelists after review closes, so the suggested generic repair does not match this workflow.
workaround: Keep these as online queries, follow cursors, and assert actual before/after score visibility and reservation privacy.
suggested_fix: Explain the difference between runtime online pagination and statically certified complete audiences, with a blind-review example.

summary: check refusals carry exact rewrites
detail: E_STRUCTURAL_FANOUT and E_QUARRY_TYPE each named the site and the fix (maintained count view; ?? 0). First fix attempt compiled, second needed one tweak.
workaround: followed the printed rewrites
suggested_fix: none

summary: detached probe tree got external SIGTERM on shared ports
detail: serve stderr shows SNAPBACK4_SIGNAL reason=SIGTERM minutes after a healthy start; whole probe group (serve+static+driver) gone while an unrelated setsid sleep survived. No output from my side explains it.
workaround: relaunch probe:serve and run reviewer checks immediately; rely on harness window for the real review
suggested_fix: nothing backend-side; shared-host port hygiene should not SIGTERM strangers

summary: Negative photo-presence probe emits an authorization warning for a display flag
detail: check emits N_UNREADABLE_PROBE for wheelList.photoDue. Wheel and photo read rules have matching cave/head audiences, but the compiler does not prove that relationship here. The flag is advisory; a unique wheel/week key enforces the actual photo limit.
workaround: Reviewed both read rules and tested the flag plus same-week constraint; retained the useful conservative warning.
suggested_fix: Recognize equivalent parent-linked audiences, or let an advisory-only expression be annotated with the reason its warning was reviewed.

summary: Sales-safe disclosure needs a publication table and explicit withdrawal
detail: The app stores private wheel care/history/photos separately from sales-visible released wheel summaries. The release job writes the summary, while rejectWheel must delete it to revoke both sales and buyer reads. This is a deliberate implementation choice rather than an observed missing backend feature.
workaround: Use a unique wheel key on the release publication, copy only label/weight/date, and test immediate withdrawal on rejection.
suggested_fix: Add an end-to-end aging/publication/withdrawal example beside the existing timed-disclosure recipes, including asset privacy.

summary: Completeness advisory does not understand the role branch in stationStatus
detail: N_NEVER_COMPLETE claims the station page lacks a code pin for crew, although the authored crew branch pins .code to the roster rig. Both acceptance runs asserted complete:true for all eight users. --verbose explains an analyzer limitation but repeats a long proposed narrowing that would break station-wide scope.
workaround: Kept the explicit crew-vs-staff branch and tested the actual complete flag. The two station rigs fit the intentional top-100 bound.
suggested_fix: Analyze each returned page under its branch conditions and shorten advisory output when a correct branched form already exists.
